q: Attackers are bombarding employees with push-notification MFA prompts at night until someone approves one out of frustration. Which change BEST reduces this risk?
c: Replace push approval with FIDO2 authenticators
Increase the minimum password length to sixteen
Deliver one-time codes over SMS instead of push
Require users to re-enroll their devices monthly

q: A hospital wants access rights assigned through job functions such as nurse or pharmacist, so that transfers between departments only require changing a user's role membership. Which access control model fits BEST?
c: Role-based access control
Discretionary access control
Mandatory access control
Rule-based access control

q: Employees access a partner's cloud application by signing in with corporate credentials through SAML federation. During this flow, which party actually authenticates the user?
c: The partner's application receiving the assertion
The company's identity provider
The SAML assertion exchanged in the flow
The user's web browser handling the redirects

q: An employee who has moved through three departments still holds access granted in every previous role. Which control MOST directly corrects this accumulation?
c: Multi-factor authentication on all accounts
Password rotation every ninety days
Periodic access reviews that recertify entitlements
Single sign-on across enterprise systems

q: In a Kerberos environment, a user authenticates once in the morning and then opens sessions to several servers all day without re-entering a password. Which component makes this possible?
c: The ticket-granting ticket issued by the key distribution center
The server's long-term secret key
The password cached on the workstation
A SAML assertion from the domain controller

q: When comparing biometric door-access systems, a vendor advertises the operating point where the false acceptance rate equals the false rejection rate. What is this metric called?
c: The false acceptance rate
The throughput rate
The failure to enroll rate
The crossover error rate

q: A global firm must let contract reviewers open documents only during business hours, only from managed devices, and only for their assigned region. Which authorization model expresses these conditions MOST naturally?
c: Role-based access control
Attribute-based access control
Mandatory access control
Per-document access control lists

q: A finance employee resigns without notice after a heated dispute with management and leaves the building immediately. From an identity and access management perspective, what should the security team do FIRST?
c: Archive the employee's mailbox and home directory to satisfy data retention requirements
Schedule an exit interview to recover the employee's badge, laptop, and other company assets
Disable all of the employee's accounts, tokens, and remote access immediately
Delete the employee's accounts so that no entitlements remain in any system

q: A security architect must select an authentication design that combines two genuinely different factor categories. Which combination satisfies the requirement for multifactor authentication?
c: A hardware one-time-password token paired with a fingerprint scan
A password paired with answers to preset security questions
A numeric PIN paired with a long passphrase
A fingerprint scan paired with facial recognition

q: A defense contractor's document system assigns classification labels to every file and clearance levels to every user. The operating system enforces the access comparison, and users cannot alter permissions even on files they created themselves. Which access control model is in use?
c: Discretionary access control
Mandatory access control
Role-based access control
Rule-based access control

q: A retailer is building a consumer mobile application backed by REST APIs and wants customers to sign in through external identity providers. The team needs a federation protocol whose tokens the APIs can parse easily on every call. Which choice is MOST appropriate?
c: SAML 2.0 with the HTTP POST browser binding
Kerberos with cross-realm trust between the parties
OAuth 2.0 using the client credentials grant
OpenID Connect issuing signed JSON Web Tokens

q: A network operations team wants centralized AAA for administering routers and switches, including authorization of individual configuration commands and encryption of the entire AAA packet payload between device and server. Which protocol BEST meets these requirements?
c: TACACS+
RADIUS
Diameter
Kerberos

q: An employee moved from accounts payable to procurement three months ago. An audit now finds the employee can both create vendor records and approve payments, a combination policy forbids. Which practice would have BEST prevented this situation?
c: Requiring multifactor authentication for both financial applications
Running an annual recertification campaign across all entitlements
A transfer workflow that revokes prior-role access when an employee changes duties
Applying immediate deprovisioning procedures for terminated employees

q: A colocation facility's server hall is protected by badge readers, but a recent assessment observed employees holding the door open for people behind them. Which control would BEST prevent unauthorized individuals from entering the hall?
c: Monitor the entrance with recorded CCTV coverage
Install an access control vestibule requiring badge and PIN to pass
Deliver security awareness training on tailgating
Review badge logs weekly for entries outside business hours

q: A bank is launching fully online account opening. The security officer notes that strong login controls are useless if a fraudster can enroll under a stolen identity in the first place. Which process addresses this concern?
c: Enrolling every new customer in multifactor authentication
Federating customer logins through a social identity provider
Enforcing strict password length and complexity at registration
Identity proofing that validates evidence such as government-issued documents before enrollment

q: A perimeter firewall evaluates every packet against an ordered list of conditions such as source address, destination port, and protocol, applying the same list to all traffic regardless of who sent it. Which access control model does this illustrate?
c: Rule-based access control
Role-based access control
Discretionary access control
Attribute-based access control

q: After a maintenance window, workstations at a branch office drift more than five minutes from the domain's key distribution center, and Kerberos authentication begins failing with invalid-ticket errors. What security purpose does this strict time requirement serve?
c: It enforces idle session timeout policies consistently across the domain
It ensures X.509 certificate validity periods are evaluated correctly
It keeps password expiration dates synchronized between realms
It bounds ticket lifetimes so captured tickets cannot be replayed later

q: A SaaS provider will let each enterprise customer authenticate its own users through the customer's identity provider and send assertions to the platform. The provider's security manager worries about account takeover. Which concern is MOST important to address in the federation agreements?
c: Customer directories will transmit user passwords to the platform during each login
Weak authentication practices at any customer identity provider become the platform's account-takeover exposure
The customer identity providers will gain the ability to read all data the platform stores
Single sign-on will prevent the platform from generating its own audit logs of user activity

q: An audit finds that 40 system administrators hold standing domain administrator rights, although each uses them only a few times per month. Which approach BEST reduces the associated risk while preserving the team's ability to operate?
c: Rotate the administrators' passwords on a monthly schedule
Consolidate the rights into one shared administrator account
Grant elevated rights just-in-time through a privileged access checkout with time limits
Forward all administrator activity to the SIEM for monitoring

q: A CISO is modernizing the corporate password standard to align with current NIST guidance on memorized secrets. Which change is consistent with that guidance?
c: Screen new passwords against known-compromised lists and drop routine forced expiration
Mandate composition rules requiring all four character classes in every password
Shorten the maximum password age so users must rotate passwords every 30 days
Add knowledge-based security questions as a mandatory secondary verification step

q: Reviewing an authorization design, an architect sees that each subject carries its own list naming the objects it may use and the rights held on each. Auditors complain that answering 'who can access this file?' requires examining every subject in the system. Which statement BEST describes the design?
c: It uses access control lists, which attach permission entries to each object
It uses security labels, which require clearance-to-classification comparison
It uses capability tables, which bind permission entries to each subject
It stores a complete access control matrix with every subject-object pairing

q: A development team proposes letting a new internal portal authenticate users by accepting any valid OAuth 2.0 access token presented to it. During architecture review, the security architect rejects the design. What is the MOST accurate basis for the objection?
c: OAuth cannot be used for federation, so the tokens must be replaced with SAML assertions
An access token conveys delegated authorization, so possessing one does not prove the user's identity
Bearer tokens cannot be replayed when sent over TLS, so the design is already acceptable
The design fails only because the access token lifetime is too long and should be shortened

q: A DevOps review discovers batch jobs that log in with service-account passwords embedded in plaintext within the scripts; the passwords have not changed in four years. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Move the passwords into an encrypted spreadsheet shared with the operations team
Rewrite the jobs to run under each administrator's personal user account
Configure the service accounts to require interactive multifactor authentication
Store the credentials in a secrets vault that rotates them and serves them to jobs via API

q: An intelligence analyst holds a Secret clearance but is denied access to a Secret-classified file belonging to a program she is not assigned to support. Which principle is being applied?
c: Need to know
Least privilege
Separation of duties
Implicit deny

q: A bank's mobile app authenticates customers with a password typed on the phone plus an approval prompt delivered to an authenticator app installed on the same phone. A risk assessment flags the design. What is the MOST significant weakness?
c: Push approval prompts do not qualify as a valid authentication factor
Push notifications travel across the internet and can be read in transit
A compromise of the single device can defeat both factors at once, undermining their independence
Customers must re-enroll the authenticator whenever they replace their phones

q: An enterprise with hundreds of SaaS subscriptions finds that account creation and removal lag weeks behind HR joiner and leaver events. The IAM team wants an open standard to automate provisioning and deprovisioning from the central directory to the SaaS providers. Which should they adopt?
c: SCIM
SAML 2.0
OAuth 2.0
LDAP

q: While engineering roles for a new ERP system, the design team must guarantee that no single user can ever hold the ability both to create a vendor and to approve payments to that vendor. Which mechanism BEST enforces this within the authorization model?
c: Dual control requiring two people to jointly execute payment approvals
Job rotation moving staff between procurement positions periodically
Least privilege provisioning of each user's individual entitlements
Mutually exclusive role constraints so the two roles can never be assigned to one user

q: A CIO proposes enterprise-wide single sign-on to reduce helpdesk password resets and user friction. The CISO supports the project but insists a specific risk be mitigated first. Which risk is MOST significant with SSO?
c: Users will need to remember more passwords, encouraging weak choices
One compromised credential or session can open every connected application
Single sign-on is incompatible with multifactor authentication
Application owners lose the ability to log the actions of signed-on users

q: During a quarterly review, an analyst discovers an enabled account belonging to a contractor whose engagement ended six months ago. The account's last successful logon was three days ago. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Delete the account to eliminate the exposure permanently
Perform root cause analysis of the deprovisioning control failure
Disable the account and preserve it while the recent activity is investigated
Contact the contractor's former sponsor to confirm the engagement status

q: A trading firm plans to roll out fingerprint authentication. The privacy officer asks the architect to explain the MOST important way biometric credentials differ from passwords when designing storage and breach response. Which response is accurate?
c: Biometric matching is exact, so stored templates require no special protection
A compromised biometric cannot be reissued, so template protection and fallback revocation options are essential
Fingerprints are classified as something you have, so adding a PIN provides no additional factor
Templates are stored as one-way hashes, so their disclosure creates no meaningful risk

q: A government agency issues employees smart cards containing a private key, and each user must enter a PIN to unlock the card before it will perform authentication. Which BEST characterizes this scheme?
c: Single-factor authentication, because the PIN is the actual credential
Two-factor authentication combining something you are with something you know
Single-factor authentication until a fingerprint reader is added to the card
Two-factor authentication combining possession of the card with knowledge of the PIN

q: In a centralized attribute-based access control deployment, an application gateway intercepts each user request, forwards the request context to a central policy engine, receives a permit or deny verdict, and then allows or blocks the request. In this architecture, what is the gateway?
c: The policy enforcement point
The policy decision point
The policy administration point
The policy information point

q: A junior engineer reviewing a new application's authorization module notices that when a user's request does not match any configured permission rule, the application grants the access and merely logs a warning. Which access control principle is the application violating?
c: Least privilege
Separation of duties
Implicit deny
Defense in depth

q: During a design review for a new customer portal, the security architect is asked how account passwords should be protected in the credential database. Which approach BEST protects the passwords against offline cracking if the database is stolen?
c: Hash each password with a unique salt using a deliberately slow adaptive function such as bcrypt or a memory-hard function such as Argon2
Encrypt all passwords with AES-256 using a key stored in a hardware security module
Hash all passwords with a single fast cryptographic hash such as SHA-256 to preserve performance
Require all passwords to be at least sixteen characters so that cracking becomes impractical

q: An audit finds that 14 employees who left the company during the past year still had active directory accounts because their managers forgot to submit termination tickets. Which remediation BEST prevents this failure from recurring?
c: Require all managers to complete annual training on the termination checklist
Integrate the directory with the HR system so employment status changes automatically trigger account deprovisioning
Increase the frequency of user access reviews from annually to quarterly
Configure all accounts to expire automatically every 90 days unless renewed

q: Incident responders determine that attackers extracted the secret of the Kerberos key distribution center's krbtgt account and have been forging ticket-granting tickets for arbitrary users. Password resets for all user accounts have already been completed. What MUST the team do to invalidate the forged tickets?
c: Reduce the maximum ticket-granting ticket lifetime so the forged tickets expire much sooner
Force all users to re-authenticate so that fresh session keys are issued to everyone
Rebuild every domain controller in the forest from known-good installation media
Reset the krbtgt account credential twice so no ticket signed with the stolen secret is honored

q: A company federates workforce access to 40 SaaS applications through its identity provider. During a control test, an account disabled at the identity provider could still use several SaaS applications for many hours afterward. Which control gap MOST likely explains this?
c: The SaaS providers are caching user passwords locally instead of deferring to the identity provider
The federation trust uses weak certificate key lengths that allow assertions to be forged
The applications rely on long-lived sessions and tokens with no revocation or logout propagation from the identity provider
The deprovisioning workflow failed to remove the user's role assignments inside each application

q: A hardware vendor's technician needs one-time access to a server room to replace a failed drive under warranty. Which approach BEST controls this physical access?
c: Issue the technician a temporary badge carrying the same access profile as data-center staff
Log the visit and have an authorized employee escort the technician for the entire time on site
Have the technician sign a nondisclosure agreement before being allowed to enter the room
Verify the technician's government identification at reception and then allow unescorted access

q: A bank uses SMS one-time codes as the second factor for customer logins. Fraud investigators report a spike in account takeovers in which attackers ported victims' phone numbers to new SIM cards. What is the BEST strategic response?
c: Migrate customers to an authenticator app or hardware token so codes no longer travel over the carrier network
Increase the length of the SMS one-time code from six digits to eight digits
Require customers to change their online banking passwords more frequently
Shorten the validity window of each SMS one-time code to thirty seconds

q: A finance application allows a user to hold both the 'create payment' and 'approve payment' roles, but the system blocks any user from approving a payment that they themselves created. Which control is being applied?
c: Static separation of duties enforced at role assignment
Least privilege enforced through role-based access control
Two-person integrity requiring simultaneous action by two employees
Dynamic separation of duties enforced at transaction time

q: Quarterly access recertifications show a 99.8 percent approval rate, and sampling reveals managers approving hundreds of entitlements within minutes, including several later confirmed to be inappropriate. As the IAM program lead, what is the BEST improvement to make?
c: Move the recertification campaigns from quarterly to monthly so inappropriate access is caught sooner
Give reviewers risk-ranked, plain-language entitlement descriptions with peer-group outlier flags, and require justification for high-risk approvals
Reassign the review responsibility from business managers to the security operations team
Automatically revoke any entitlement the reviewer has not explicitly approved by the campaign deadline

q: An enterprise deploys IEEE 802.1X port-based network access control. A laptop's supplicant submits credentials that are carried through the wired switch to a central server. In this architecture, which component actually decides whether the laptop is granted network access?
c: The authentication server that evaluates the credentials against the identity store
The switch acting as the authenticator on the access port
The supplicant software running on the connecting laptop
The DHCP server that issues the laptop its network configuration

q: An agency is designing digital identity requirements for three online services: viewing public park hours, filing personal tax information, and approving high-value grant disbursements. The CISO rejects a proposal to require in-person identity proofing and hardware authenticators for all three. Which principle supports the CISO's position?
c: Defense in depth requires layered controls rather than strong authentication alone
Usability must always take precedence over security in citizen-facing services
Identity and authenticator assurance levels should be selected per service based on the risk and impact of a failure
Strong authentication is unnecessary because the sensitive services already encrypt data in transit

q: A project manager creates a folder on the collaboration platform and personally decides which colleagues receive read or edit rights, adding and removing people as she sees fit. Which access control model is the platform implementing?
c: Mandatory access control
Discretionary access control
Role-based access control
Attribute-based access control

q: A hospital maintains a 'break-glass' administrator account so clinicians and engineers can obtain emergency access if the identity system fails during a patient-safety event. Which set of controls BEST governs this account?
c: Disable the account entirely and require the on-call director to create a fresh one during each emergency
Distribute the account password to all senior staff so that an emergency never delays access
Protect the account with the same multifactor authentication required for routine administrator logins
Store the credential sealed, alert on any use, and review then rotate it after every activation

q: A red team reports that any authenticated domain user can request Kerberos service tickets for accounts with registered service principal names and crack the encrypted tickets offline, recovering several service-account passwords. What is the MOST effective remediation?
c: Replace the vulnerable accounts with managed service accounts or long, random, machine-generated passwords
Configure account lockout to block accounts after a small number of failed logon attempts
Restrict the ability to request service tickets to members of a dedicated service operators group
Shorten the service ticket lifetime so that any cracked ticket expires within a few hours

q: Auditors find that six database administrators all log in to production servers using one shared 'dbadmin' account, making it impossible to attribute changes to individuals. Which remediation BEST restores accountability?
c: Require the shared password to be changed every 30 days and immediately after any administrator departs
Enable verbose logging of every command executed under the shared dbadmin account
Issue each administrator a unique privileged account requiring elevation, and remove direct shared logins
Require administrators to record each use of dbadmin in a sign-out spreadsheet

q: During a penetration test of a SAML-federated procurement portal, testers modify the username inside an intercepted assertion, replay it to the service provider, and are logged in as the altered user. What is the ROOT cause of this vulnerability?
c: The identity provider issued the assertion over an unencrypted transport channel
The service provider fails to properly validate the digital signature covering the assertion
The assertion validity lifetime is too long, allowing it to be replayed after it should have expired
The identity provider did not require multifactor authentication before issuing the assertion

q: A retail website lets customers reset forgotten passwords by answering their mother's maiden name and the name of their first pet. Why is this design considered weak?
c: The answers are too difficult for legitimate customers to remember accurately over time
Security questions count as a biometric factor and therefore can never be changed
The reset process fails to notify customers by email whenever it has been used
The answers are often discoverable from social media and public records, so they rest on knowledge attackers can obtain

q: A managed services provider needs system accounts for a nine-month implementation project. Historically, similar third-party accounts have remained active for years after their projects ended. Which provisioning practice BEST addresses this risk?
c: Create the accounts with expiration dates tied to the contract end and require a named sponsor to renew them
Grant the provider one shared account so there is only a single credential to remember to remove
Add the provider's accounts to the population covered by the quarterly access review
Require the provider to commit contractually to reporting its staff departures promptly

q: A network capture during an internal assessment shows several applications sending user credentials to the corporate directory as LDAP simple binds in cleartext. What should the security team require?
c: Replace the directory service entirely with a Kerberos key distribution center
Move the directory server into a separate VLAN so packet captures become harder
Require LDAPS or StartTLS so that all binds occur over an encrypted channel
Hash each password on the client before it is sent in the bind request

q: A global firm wants stronger login security, but the workforce complains that entering a one-time code at every single login is burdensome. Which authentication strategy BEST balances risk reduction and user friction?
c: Drop the second factor entirely for all users and compensate by forcing password changes every 30 days
Adopt risk-based authentication that steps up to additional factors only when signals such as device, location, or behavior look anomalous
Require the one-time code only for administrators and IT staff, exempting the general workforce from a second factor
Extend the session and token lifetimes so that each user only has to authenticate about once per month

q: Five years after deploying role-based access control, an enterprise has 11,000 roles for 9,000 employees; many roles have a single member, and administrators create a new role for nearly every access request. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Run a role engineering effort combining top-down business analysis with bottom-up entitlement mining to consolidate roles, using attributes for exceptions
Freeze all new role creation immediately and maintain the freeze until the total role count falls below the number of employees
Abandon the role model entirely and grant all future access through direct, individual user-level permission assignments
Migrate every existing role unchanged into a new identity governance platform so the roles can at least be centrally reported

q: A terminated engineer's network accounts were disabled within minutes, yet he entered the office with his badge three days later because the physical access system is administered separately by the facilities team. What is the BEST long-term correction?
c: Post security guards at every entrance to visually verify that each entrant is a current employee
Require the facilities team to reconcile the badge holder list against HR records once each month
Shorten badge validity so that every employee badge must be re-enabled at reception each week
Manage badge credentials through the same identity lifecycle processes that drive logical account deprovisioning

q: Employees connecting to corporate Wi-Fi have had credentials harvested by rogue access points broadcasting the corporate network name. The current design uses username and password over a protocol where clients frequently ignore server certificate warnings. What is the BEST fix?
c: Hide the SSID broadcast and filter wireless connections by client MAC address
Deploy certificate-based mutual authentication such as EAP-TLS so clients verify the network before presenting anything
Require employees to change their Wi-Fi passwords whenever a rogue access point is detected nearby
Increase the wireless encryption strength from AES-128 to AES-256 on all corporate access points

q: A mid-sized company plans to move all workforce authentication to a cloud identity-as-a-service provider fronting every business application. From a risk-management perspective, which consideration is MOST important to evaluate before committing?
c: Whether the provider's login interface can be rebranded with the company's logo and color scheme
Whether the provider supports importing the company's existing password hashes during migration
The provider's availability history, contractual service levels, and the company's contingency plan if the service is unreachable
Whether the per-user subscription cost is lower than operating the current on-premises directory

q: After enabling a policy that locks accounts for 24 hours after three failed logins, a trading firm suffers an attack in which someone deliberately fails logins against hundreds of known usernames, locking most traders out during market hours. Which redesign BEST balances the competing risks?
c: Keep the hard lockout policy in place but reduce the lockout duration from 24 hours to one hour
Remove the failed-login limit entirely and rely on password complexity rules to resist guessing attacks
Suppress all username hints and error details so attackers cannot confirm which accounts actually exist
Replace hard lockout with progressive delays and risk-based blocking of suspicious sources, backed by MFA and monitoring
